compute_expectation.implication: two 120-game direct lanes are expected to be tens of seconds, not compute-bound against a 30-minute cadence; unverified on the remote machine
compute_expectation.source_measurement: Phase 16 full 120-board direct pack ran in 0.2 minutes (12 s) at 10 workers on the M4 Pro
compute_expectation.source_measurement_phase17: the real 240-game composite (both lanes) took 22.9 s at 4 workers on the M4 Pro

identified_risks.impact: evaluator cannot run, or runs with different float behaviour
identified_risks.resolution: python3.13 and uv are already installed on the MacBook; no interpreter download needed. torch 2.13.0 and numpy 2.5.1 will be pinned to match the source.
identified_risks.risk: remote PyTorch absent, or x86_64 under Rosetta

identified_risks.impact: same candidate scores differently on the two machines; a silent false result
identified_risks.mitigation: contract section 5 cross-machine identity fixture before the full pack
identified_risks.resolution: phase17_cross_machine_fixture_v1 built and self-tested with six negative controls; it compares identities, 120 setup fingerprints, whole-game action sequences and float32 logits. Measurement needs the MacBook.
identified_risks.risk: cross-machine float divergence flips a greedy opponent argmax and changes whole games

identified_risks.impact: missed slots; backlog must stay bound to original candidates, never re-attributed
identified_risks.risk: host sleep or network loss during the 13 h window

identified_risks.mitigation: Agent 4 writes through a .partial temp name and os.replace; Agent 5 stages remotely the same way
identified_risks.risk: transport reads a partially written file

identified_risks.impact: the worker stops mid-run; backlog grows
identified_risks.mitigation: every worker failure emits a refusal receipt, so exhaustion is visible to Agent 7 rather than silent
identified_risks.risk: remote disk exhaustion during the run (12 GiB free, 8 GB RAM, macOS swap)

identified_risks.impact: cross-machine result comparison would have been impossible
identified_risks.mitigation: result_digest now covers a scoring-only projection; verified reproducible across two independent runs
identified_risks.risk: result_digest folded a wall-clock field, so the same bundle digested differently run to run

install_permission.choice: user-local only; no admin, nothing outside the home directory
install_permission.consequence: Homebrew python3.13 and uv are already present, so NO interpreter download is required

transport_topology.choice: authenticated pull - the MacBook connects in and pulls
transport_topology.operator_constraint: operator initially preferred the machines not connect; the SSH surface was narrowed to a single forced command in response

rejected.icloud_shared_storage: operator's stated second preference; not chosen
rejected.manual_airdrop_usb: contract permits it for the h0 gate only, never unattended production

worker_count.basis: matches the 4 performance cores; leaves headroom in 8 GB

one_time_static_payload.note: seven rule/stress opponents are code, not weights; the composite pack is expected to carry setup bytes so the 8,000-board accepted setup library need NOT be shipped

payload_sizing.per_candidate_basis: move EMA 863,959 params + setup EMA 802,320 params, float32, plus manifest
payload_sizing.remote_headroom_note: ~900 MB needed against ~12 GiB free: fits, but 12 GiB free on an 8 GB-RAM machine that will swap is thin. Recommended, not required: free some space before the run.

source_machine.remote_login: OFF; operator must enable it (system setting, not Agent 5's to change)

ssh_design.authorized_key_written_by: the operator, not Agent 5 - granting machine access is the operator's action
ssh_design.key: dedicated ed25519, no passphrase, used for nothing else
ssh_design.residual_risk: enabling Remote Login also permits password SSH for the account from the LAN; hardening that means editing /etc/ssh/sshd_config with sudo, which is the operator's decision and password, not Agent 5's
